title: The resurrection and the life
hookLine: Jesus tells Martha: I am the resurrection and the life (John 11:25)

lines: MARTHA GOES OUT TO MEET HIM.
cards: A house in Bethany, near Jerusalem. A man named Lazarus has died. His sisters, Martha and Mary, had sent word to their friend Jesus while Lazarus was still sick.
He came late. By the time he arrives, John's Gospel says, Lazarus has lain in the grave four days. Martha hears that Jesus is on the road and goes out to meet him; Mary stays in the house.
Martha's first words are the ones a grieving person says at a hospital door: "Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died."

teach.h: MARTHA HOPES FOR THE LAST DAY.

teach.b: When Jesus tells her that her brother will rise again, she answers with what she knows: "I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day." Her hope is real, but far away, at the end of everything.
It doesn't help much on day fifteen. Jesus answers: "I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live."
In John's telling, the hope Martha placed at the end of time is standing in front of her on a dusty road, with a name and a face.
Then he asks her plainly: "Believest thou this?" Martha says yes, and names him the Christ. On the way to the tomb, before anything is mended, come two words: "Jesus wept."
Only after the weeping does he call, "Lazarus, come forth," and the dead man walks out still wrapped in grave clothes. Christians read this as a sign, a return to this life.
The hope they hold is larger: that because Jesus himself rose from the dead, the dead will be raised.
Churches describe the details in their own ways, and in some churches this line is read at funerals and spoken at gravesides.

teach.h: A WEEK OF ANSWERS TO DEATH.
teach.b: Look back at the week: Nachiketa at Death's door, the fires on the ghats, a mourner's prayer of praise, neighbors who come to the house, numbered days, a time for everything.
And today, one tradition's hope said out loud, whether or not it's yours.

how: Some churches read John 11 at funerals, and in some burial services the words "I am the resurrection, and the life" are spoken at the graveside.

games.q: you're Martha. your brother is four days in the grave and the friend you sent for has finally come. what do you do?
o: stay in the house and refuse to see him.
go out to meet him and say, if you had been here.
send a message telling him not to bother.
games.why: Martha goes out on the road, says it plainly, and hears: I am the resurrection, and the life.

practice: Hear Martha's first line again, if you had been here, the sentence of anyone who arrived too late or watched someone else arrive too late.

Then hear the answer in John's Gospel, I am the resurrection, and the life, and let it sit beside her grief, the hope and the tears in the same scene. If you pray, you can carry Martha's words into the quiet.
